specification.title: A migration that provides no reversal is reverted
steps: Runner A applies { m1 }. m1 inserts marker m1 and provides no reversal.
Revert with the framework's default selection.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the revert has returned and the reapply has returned: the runner records the state at report time.

invariants.statement: If a revert reports a migration as reverted, its history entry is absent and its marker is absent.

If a migration provides no reversal, a revert does not report it as reverted while its marker remains: it refuses before changing history, or follows a documented irreversible-migration contract that keeps history and database consistent.

execution.description: Positive control. Explicit BEGIN, parameterized writes, COMMIT or ROLLBACK. PG::Result#cmd_status of COMMIT must be COMMIT before the control reports committed. A tag of ROLLBACK is reported as rolled back. Any other tag, or a COMMIT that raises, is reported as failed. A failed ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT is followed by ROLLBACK, not COMMIT. A connection whose ROLLBACK failed is closed. BEGIN carries a requested isolation level. One PG::Connection, or a one-connection holder for TX-03. Not a framework pool.

configuration.commit_reply: cmd_status checked; only COMMIT is a commit, only ROLLBACK is a rollback

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

knowledge: The caller of revert learns only what the operation reports. If that report says the migration was reverted, the caller treats its effects as gone.

api_outcome.basis: the migration has no reversal, so the control refused
api_outcome.contract: The correct control runs a migration in one transaction. It takes a transaction-scoped advisory lock before it reads history, applies the migration only when history has no entry, and commits the marker and the history entry together. A reversal deletes the marker and the history entry, refuses a migration that has no reversal, and rolls back a reversal that raises.
